paper_assessment.supporting_quote: Interactions of metabolites of MDMA, methylone and MDPV with human monoaminergic systems were assessed. METHODS: The ability of parent drugs and their metabolites to inhibit uptake of tritiated norepinephrine, dopamine and serotonin (5-HT) was assessed in human embryonic kidney 293 cells transfected with human monoamine transporters. Binding affinities and functional activity at monoamine transporters and various receptor subtypes were also determined. RESULTS: MDMA and methylone displayed greater potency to inhibit norepinephrine uptake as compared to their effects on dopamine and 5-HT uptake.
paper_assessment.reasoning_summary: The paper investigates the mechanistic interactions of MDMA, methylone, MDPV, and their metabolites with human monoaminergic systems using in vitro assays. This directly supports primary mechanistic claims for in-scope compounds.
